edition.witness_note: Lake 1912 Loeb copy-text; Lightfoot/Funk middle recension not yet locked as second witness

source_text: [1] Ἐάν με καταξιώσῃ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν καὶ θέλημα ᾖ, ἐν τῷ δευτέρῳ βιβλιδίῳ, ὃ μέλλω γράφειν ὑμῖν, προσδηλώσω ὑμῖν, ἦς ἠρξάμην οἰκονομίας εἰς τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν, ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ πίστει καὶ ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ ἀγάπῃ, ἐν πάθει αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστάσει: [2] μάλιστα ἐὰν ὁ κύριός μοι ἀποκαλύψῃ, ὅτι οἱ κατ’ ἄνδρα κοινῇ πάντες ἐν χάριτι ἐξ ὀνόματος συνέρχεσθε ἐν μιᾷ πίστει καὶ ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ. τῷ κατὰ σάρκα ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ, τῷ υἱῷ ἀνθρώπου καὶ υἱῷ θεοῦ, εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν ὑμᾶς τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ἀπερισπάστῳ διανοίᾳ, ἕνα ἄρτον κλῶντες, ὅς ἐστιν φάρμακον ἀθανασίας, ἀντίδοτος τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν, ἀλλὰ ζῆν ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ διὰ παντός.
pass_a_gloss: If Jesus Christ counts me worthy through your prayer, and if it is his will, in the second little book which I intend to write to you I will further explain to you the plan which I began concerning the new man Jesus Christ, in his faith and in his love, in his suffering and resurrection; especially if the Lord reveals to me that you, each and all in common, by grace from his name, come together in one faith and in Jesus Christ, who according to the flesh is of the family of David, Son of Man and Son of God, so that you obey the bishop and the presbytery with an undistracted mind, breaking one bread, which is the medicine of immortality, an antidote so that we do not die but live in Jesus Christ forever.
pass_b_english: If Jesus Christ counts me worthy through your prayer, and if it is his will, then in the second little book I mean to write you, I will explain further the plan I began to set out about the New Man, Jesus Christ (Ephesians 2:15): in his faith and in his love, in his suffering and in his resurrection.

I will do so above all if the Lord shows me that every one of you, together, by the grace that comes from his Name, is gathering in one faith and in Jesus Christ, who in the flesh was of David's line (Romans 1:3), the Son of Man and the Son of God. You gather so that you may obey the bishop and the presbytery with an undistracted mind, breaking one bread (1 Corinthians 10:16-17). That bread is the medicine of immortality, an antidote against death, so that we do not die but live in Jesus Christ forever (John 6:50-51).

choices.term: φάρμακον ἀθανασίας, ἀντίδοτος τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν
choices.english: the medicine of immortality, the antidote that keeps us from dying
choices.why: Ignatius's famous medical image kept whole; φάρμακον is a drug or remedy.

choices.term: εἰς τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν
choices.why: Here a title of Christ (from Ephesians 2:15), so capitalized under the divine-titles rule.
rejected: the new man (lowercase; reads as generic)

choices.term: ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ πίστει καὶ ἐν τῇ αὐτοῦ ἀγάπῃ
choices.english: in his faith and in his love
choices.why: αὐτοῦ is parallel to ἐν πάθει αὐτοῦ καὶ ἀναστάσει; kept as 'his' so the genitive is not narrowed to faith in him / love for him.
rejected: faith in him and love for him (objective genitive; narrows)

choices.term: οἱ κατ’ ἄνδρα κοινῇ πάντες ἐν χάριτι ἐξ ὀνόματος
choices.english: every one of you, together, by the grace that comes from his Name
choices.why: ἐξ ὀνόματος may mean 'by name, individually' (Lightfoot) or 'from the Name'. With κατ’ ἄνδρα already saying 'each', the Name reading avoids a doublet.

anf_compare.notes: Sense aligned. ANF doubles 'man by man ... individually' and reads ἐξ ὀνόματος as 'individually'; we take it as grace from the Name (noted). ANF supplies '[which causes]' where the Greek has a simple contrast, not dying but living.

bible_refs.note: εἰς ἕνα καινὸν ἄνθρωπον: the one new man
ἐκ σπέρματος Δαυὶδ κατὰ σάρκα; Ignatius κατὰ σάρκα ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ
τὸν ἄρτον ὃν κλῶμεν ... εἷς ἄρτος
bread from heaven, so that one may eat and not die (μὴ ἀποθάνῃ) ... will live forever

notes: Whole chapter 20 (sections 1-2) matches the ANF span.
The promised second book is not extant.

checker_dispute: checker b objects to inline Scripture references in Pass B. They are not presented as Ignatius's words; the library's hard rule (TRANSLATION_QA.md, 'Inline in Pass B') requires a parenthetical citation beside each clear allusion, e.g. καινὸν ἄνθρωπον (Ephesians 2:15), κατὰ σάρκα ἐκ γένους Δαυείδ (Romans 1:3), ἕνα ἄρτον κλῶντες (1 Corinthians 10:16-17), τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν, ἀλλὰ ζῆν (John 6:50-51).

review.notes: Checked paragraph [1] clause by clause. Greek Ἐάν με καταξιώσῃ Ἰησοῦς Χριστὸς ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ ὑμῶν καὶ θέλημα ᾖ … προσδηλώσω ὑμῖν, ἦς ἠρξάμην οἰκονομίας εἰς τὸν καινὸν ἄνθρωπον Ἰησοῦν Χριστόν is kept in A as 'If Jesus Christ counts me worthy through your prayer, and if it is his will … I will further explain to you the plan which I began concerning the new man Jesus Christ' and in B without a new agent or dropped condition. μάλιστα ἐὰν ὁ κύριός μοι ἀποκαλύψῃ … συνέρχεσθε … εἰς τὸ ὑπακούειν ὑμᾶς τῷ ἐπισκόπῳ καὶ τῷ πρεσβυτερίῳ ἀπερισπάστῳ διανοίᾳ, ἕνα ἄρτον κλῶντες, ὅς ἐστιν φάρμακον ἀθανασίας, ἀντίδοτος τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν, ἀλλὰ ζῆν ἐν Ἰησοῦ Χριστῷ διὰ παντός matches A's 'especially if the Lord reveals to me … breaking one bread, which is the medicine of immortality, an antidote so that we do not die but live in Jesus Christ forever' and B's same purpose, negation, and bread predicate. B's parentheticals sit on the supplied allusions (Ephesians 2:15; Romans 1:3; 1 Corinthians 10:16-17; John 6:50-51). Title names φάρμακον ἀθανασίας, not only the locus.

Source identity: Locked Greek is Ignatius Ephesians 20, matching named edition. Completeness: all clauses from the single Greek paragraph are present in both Pass A and Pass B. Negation: Greek 'τοῦ μὴ ἀποθανεῖν' rendered as 'so that we do not die' in Pass A and 'an antidote against death, so that we do not die' in Pass B — preserved. Agency: Jesus Christ as subject of 'counts me worthy', 'reveals', and 'live in Jesus Christ' — preserved. Modality: conditional 'if' clauses (Ἐάν..., ἐὰν...) rendered with 'if' in both Pass A and Pass B — preserved. Doctrine: Christological titles ('Son of Man', 'Son of God'), ecclesiology (obey bishop and presbytery), and eucharistic theology ('one bread... medicine of immortality') — preserved. Scripture: Pass B includes parenthetical citations (Ephesians 2:15, Romans 1:3, 1 Corinthians 10:16-17, John 6:50-51) as required by library rule; each matches the allusions in the Greek. Title: 'The medicine of immortality' names the central theological thought, not just a locus. Notes: disclose that the promised second book is not extant and OCR/stanza alignment is intact. No uncertainties remain.
